scope: Audit which Hearthstone semantic classes most often create false lowering from source contracts into HSConfig runtime surfaces, especially mistaken writes to Mulligan.json, per-card CardID JSON, GlobalValues.json, and Combo.json.
source_backed_findings: Start of Game effects resolve before the mulligan, so start-of-game text is not evidence that a card must be kept in the opening hand; HSConfig already encodes this split in its README, source-document surface gates, mulligan planner, and Darkbishop Benedictus regressions.

Deckbuilding effects trigger during deck creation rather than during mulligan or normal card play. Highlander, odd-even deck checks, and deck-size modifiers therefore describe deck-state legality or pre-game conditions, not direct mulligan intent.

In-deck effects are exceptional rules, and quest-style guaranteed starters are a special mulligan rule rather than a generic start-of-game or deckbuilding rule. They need dedicated handling instead of broad lowering from generic text families.

Discover and Choose One are explicit choice mechanics. Runtime-lowerable behavior depends on resolving the chosen option identity, which matches HSConfig's dedicated discover_choice and choose_one_choice handling instead of generic mechanic lowering.

Hero-power transforms are a distinct runtime concern. HSConfig already routes hero_power_transform to BeforeUseHeroPowerBonus and keeps it off Mulligan and Combo surfaces unless separate opening-hand evidence exists.

Generated entities are not all equivalent. Deterministic chosen results, deterministic entourage links, and random pools must stay separate; HSConfig's static semantics already distinguishes generated_entity from generated_entity_random_pool for this reason.

Secrets, Locations, and Weapons all carry temporal or board-state semantics that are richer than simple static tags: Secrets are hidden delayed triggers, Locations are repeated free activations on later turns, and Weapons create equip plus repeated attack-turn behavior.

Combo sequences are ordered multi-card claims in HSConfig and should lower only from explicit combo_sequence evidence, not from generic archetype prose, card-role descriptions, or vague 'finisher' language.

Modern Wild mechanics increase false-lowering pressure because they mix deckbuilding, hero-power replacement, generated rewards, or multi-ability activations. Tourist, Titan, Imbue, Forge, and Excavate are current examples of mechanics that should first enrich the contract and only later gain dedicated lowering if a stable surface exists.
repo_implications: Keep claim kind as the first runtime authority boundary. Explicit mulligan_keep or mulligan_discard should remain the only direct route into Mulligan.json.
Preserve the current start-of-game suppression rule: effect-only start_of_game or hero_power_transform cards may enrich per-card behavior and reports without becoming opening-hand keeps by inference.
Continue routing option mechanics through identity resolution. If a Discover or Choose One option cannot be resolved to an option card id, suppress runtime lowering and keep the claim report-visible.

Treat deckbuilding modifiers, highlander rules, odd-even checks, deck-size modifiers, and start-in-deck requirements as contract evidence first. Only lower them when a runtime surface and explicit claim kind are both well-defined.

Prefer per-card CardID behavior rows for targeting, hero-power use, discover-choice resolution, weapon posture, and other card-local timing semantics instead of trying to encode them in GlobalValues.json.
Keep random generation, secret timing, location activation, and unsupported modern mechanics in report-only or suppressed lanes until a deterministic runtime mapping and regression fixture exist.

Expand semantic micro-fixtures and source fixtures around quest-style guaranteed starters, generated random pools, Titan activations, Tourist deckbuilding, and Imbue hero-power replacement so new mechanics are tested as boundaries rather than patched ad hoc.
correctness_risks: A start-of-game enabler can be falsely lowered into Mulligan.json if generic 'keep' prose or card importance is treated as opening-hand intent.
Deckbuilding modifiers can be misclassified as live runtime behavior, causing odd-even, Highlander, or deck-size text to leak into the wrong surface.
Targeting claims can land on the wrong behavior block if battlecry targeting, hero-power usage, attack posture, and generic spell targeting are collapsed together.
A Discover or Choose One claim can become technically wrong if HSConfig emits a generic row without resolved option identity or lets a generic discover fallback override a specific resolved option.
Generated-card or generated-entity text can become false deterministic runtime logic if random pools are treated like fixed entourage outputs.
Combo prose can become invalid Combo.json output if ordered cards, timing, or minimum segment requirements are inferred from narrative descriptions instead of explicit combo_sequence evidence.
Secret timing, location activations, and weapon attack sequencing can be over-lowered into broad mechanic rows that miss hidden triggers, charge counts, activation cadence, or attack-turn posture.
Modern Wild mechanics such as Titan, Imbue, Tourist, Forge, and Excavate can be mislowered when text heuristics assume they behave like older single-surface keywords instead of multi-state mechanics.
slimness_risks: Adding a new runtime writer or bespoke lowering lane for every new keyword would bloat HSConfig faster than the runtime surfaces can justify.
Growing a giant keyword-to-surface allowlist without identity or timing checks would duplicate logic that is already cleaner at the claim-kind and suppression layers.
Encoding the same semantic idea across Mulligan, GlobalValues, CardID, and Combo surfaces would create overlapping authority and harder-to-debug regressions.
Using card-specific exceptions for each modern Wild outlier would make the system less maintainable than extending semantic families and surface tests.
Trying to convert unresolved or low-confidence semantics into runtime rows to look 'complete' would expand code and still produce worse outputs than a thin, explicit suppression report.
Pulling warning-only mechanics into the apply-critical path would create more gate logic without improving the load-safe package contract.
autonomy_risks: If unsupported semantics are treated as blockers, valid decks with secrets, locations, random generation, or newer mechanics could fail to produce a load-safe package even when the unsupported part is non-critical.
If every modern keyword requires manual research before any package can be produced, the any-deck workflow stops being autonomous.
If unresolved option identity or random-pool ambiguity is treated as fatal instead of report-only, autonomy degrades on discover-heavy and generation-heavy decks.
If surface gates are loosened to avoid suppression, HSConfig may appear more autonomous while actually writing more false runtime logic.
If surface gates are tightened too aggressively, whole card classes can become unlowerable even when explicit guide-backed mulligan, combo, or targeting evidence exists.

If unsupported semantics spill into apply authority instead of staying visible in operator reports, the system becomes over-conservative and blocks decks for evidence gaps that should remain advisory.
recommended_design_position: Keep HSConfig conservative, surface-specific, and non-blocking: claim kind plus resolved option identity should control runtime lowering; start-of-game, deckbuilding, generated-pool, and modern-keyword semantics should enrich the source contract first; and unsupported or random-state mechanics should remain report-visible but apply-safe until a dedicated runtime mapping with focused regression tests is proven.
